pip-sat.alt: Pip the small sandy-brown sparrow sits by himself on bare earth, filling most of the picture, with a bright sun in the corner of a clear sky.
Pip perches on the spout of an old brass tap fixed to a low brick garden wall, with a single drip of water hanging from the end of the spout.
Close up on the tap. Pip leans in and taps the metal with his beak while three drips fall below him at different heights, and rings spread across the puddle underneath.
Pip pats the puddle with one foot, delighted and a little bit naughty, sending bright water rings and splashes across the puddle in front of a brick wall.
A wide view of Pip sitting back in the sunny puddle he has made, thoroughly wet and very pleased with himself, with a trail of wet footprints leading away across the paving.

pip-and-the-tin.alt: Pip the sparrow sits neatly inside an old dented biscuit tin lying on its side in the grass, only his head and tufted crown showing over the rim.
The same tin seen from a low angle so it looms large, with Pip's surprised face and braced feet peering over the rim.
Pip stands on top of an upturned tin, drumming it with both feet, the tin wobbling beneath him while a startled ladybird takes off nearby.
Pip is curled up fast asleep inside the tin, his head tucked under one wing, warm evening light slanting in through the tin's open end.
A wide view of the whole dusk garden: the tin small beside the shed, a contented sparrow-shaped bump sleeping inside it, with the first star of the evening above the roof.

dot-the-dog.alt: Pip the small sparrow perches on a fence post beside Dot, an enormous soppy brown dog with a white patch over one eye — the size difference between them is the whole joke.
Dot the dog sits square on the grass in the classic obedient pose, tail sweeping a fan-shape through the daisies, tongue out.
Dot is squashed onto a small stripy doormat far too little for her, paws hanging off every side, while Pip watches from the doorstep looking thoroughly unimpressed.
Pip stands on Dot's broad head, patting her gently between the ears with one wing, while Dot's eyes are shut tight in absolute bliss.
Dot digs furiously with her back end in the air, earth flying in an arc behind her out of a growing hole, while Pip leaps clear of the flying soil.
Dot is fast asleep in the sunny hole she dug, with Pip asleep against her side, both rising and falling together in the late golden light.

fig-and-the-fuss.alt: A wide view of the whole garden at sunrise: a vegetable patch, the round pond, a mossy log, the old oak, and the sun just clearing the fence.
Fig the caterpillar and Ned the duckling dig side by side in the soft earth of the vegetable patch, soil flying everywhere, both of them covered in it.
Nell the bee flies in a wobbly line towards a mossy log, a few loose petals drifting in her wake.
Moss the hedgehog is fast asleep on his back in a warm patch of sun, spikes flat and utterly relaxed.
Ned is mid-tantrum, wings out and beak wide, feathers puffed up and drawn bigger than everyone else so the fuss feels enormous.
Fig holds out one small leg towards Ned, calm and patient, while Ned — still cross — is half-turned towards him.
Ned sits quietly beside Fig on the log, still muddy but smiling now, their shoulders touching.
The whole cast — Fig, Ned, Moss and Nell — sit together at the edge of the pond in the morning sun, the water like glass, everyone facing the light.

ned-and-the-fish.alt: Ned the duckling holds up a small fishing net on a bamboo cane far too long for him, the handle wobbling wildly.
Ned runs full pelt down the bank towards the pond, his fishing net trailing behind him and the grass flattening in his wake.
Looking down into the clear pond, a bright red fish hangs suspended in the water while Ned's astonished face peers down from the bank above.
The red fish darts through the water in a sharp zigzag, a trail of bubbles marking its path, while Ned watches wide-eyed from the water's edge.
Ned holds the net up triumphantly with the red fish inside it, water streaming out through the mesh, chest out and prouder than he has ever been.
Pip and Nell arrive at speed from opposite sides, both mid-flight, converging on Ned in the middle.
Pip, Ned and Nell have their heads together in close conference over the net, the fish visible between them looking distinctly unhappy.
Ned tips the net gently towards the water, the fish sliding out, his face careful and serious after all the earlier excitement.
The fish dives away with a big bright splash of water thrown up, and Ned is left soaked and laughing on the bank.
Pip, Ned and Nell sit in a row on the bank at golden hour, feet in the water, the empty net laid down beside them, warm and satisfied.

rain-on-the-oak.alt: Pip stands on a fence rail looking up at a huge green oak tree in full summer leaf, which fills most of the page in fresh, wet greens.
A close view of a single wet leaf high in the oak, the canopy filling the background, with a small round beetle sitting on the leaf, its shell shining.
A night scene with the oak dark against a deep blue sky and rain falling in long silver lines across the whole picture.
A goat stands patiently in the field beside the oak the morning after the rain, with drips still falling from the branches onto its back.
A close view of the goat's soaked coat, fur parted into wet points with water beading and running, looking thoroughly resigned.
Pip looks down from a branch at Ned in a small wooden boat on the pond far below, seen from above.
Ned sails his little boat with a leaf hoisted as a sail, steering with great concentration as the wind fills it.
A close, low view shows Ned's orange webbed feet clearly paddling through the clear shallow water beside his boat.
Pip and Ned sit side by side on the upturned boat on the bank, both dripping wet, with a bright rainbow over the oak behind them.

the-dark-farm.alt: A wide night view of the whole dark farm: the barn, a farm gate and a field of corn under a deep blue sky with almost no light yet.
Pip stands small on a gatepost, looking up at a large bright full moon that fills much of the sky.
The same moon is drawn tiny at the very top of a mostly empty sky, with the whole farm just a thin dark strip along the bottom of the page.
A fox slips low and quick between the corn stalks, its brush held straight out behind it, only partly visible through the stems.
The fox trots away with a corn cob held in its mouth, glancing back at the reader with a look of complete innocence.
Ned sits on a rock pulling off a wellington boot, leaning right back with the effort, tongue out.
Ned lowers his bare orange foot into a clear cool pool, ripples spreading outward, his face full of pure relief.
First light breaks pale green-gold along the horizon behind the barn, the moon still faintly visible above. Quiet and hopeful.
Pip and Ned sit on the farm gate as the sun rises behind them, warm gold light flooding across the fields.

the-owl-and-the-cow.alt: Olive the plum-coloured owl sits up on a branch high in the oak, round and dignified, her big amber eyes looking straight at the reader.
A wide dusk view of the whole farmyard going blue and cool, with lit windows in the farmhouse and the oak standing dark against the sky.
A large gentle cow stands in the yard beside the barn, seen from low down so she looks enormous against the cool blue night.
Ned stands with his head tilted right over, one flipper cupped by his ear, listening intently, with the cow drawn small in the distance behind him.
A close portrait of the cow's calm, characterful face with a fine pair of curved horns, her breath steaming in the cold air.
Pip peers down at a small round coin half buried in dark soil, one bright edge catching the moonlight.
Pip, Ned and Olive stand together at a farm gate at night, determined little silhouettes facing forward together.
Ned sits on an old wooden kitchen chair left out in the yard, his feet not reaching the ground, entirely at home.
A wide winter night over the farmyard: frost on the ground, bare branches, and the barn's single lit window the only warm thing in the picture.
Pip and Olive sit together on their branch, looking peacefully down at the cow far below with the whole farmyard laid out beneath them.

ned-in-the-frost.alt: Pip and Ned set off across a frosted field at first light, small against a wide pale winter sky, with their breath showing in the cold.
Pip and Ned lean hard into a strong cold wind, feathers and down blown flat backwards.
An extreme close-up of frost crystals along a single blade of grass, drawn like tiny white ferns. Beautiful and quiet, with no characters in shot.
A low, ground-level view of Pip and Ned's feet on stiff white frosted grass, the grass visibly crunching flat under them.
A twig snaps underfoot, shown as the break itself with two split ends and a spray of frost, while Ned leaps into the air with fright.
Ned crouches at the near bank of the frozen-edged pond, tail up, coiled and about to launch across to the far bank.
Ned belly-flops into the cold water with an enormous flat splash, only his tail and one foot above the surface, while Pip's beak hangs open in horror.
Pip hauls on Ned's flipper from the bank with both feet braced, absolutely straining, while Ned comes half out of the water plastered with mud.
Pip and Ned sit side by side on the frosty bank, Ned soaked and steaming faintly, both grinning as a low winter sun breaks through.

a-sunny-day.alt: A wide, bleached-bright summer scene over a farm field under a huge white-hot sun, the light almost too bright to look at.
Pip and Ned run side by side through the field, wings and flippers out in pure joy, grass seeds flying up around them.
A tall stack of golden hay bales, with Ned scrambling up the side, his feet slipping on the loose straw.
Pip is sunk deep into loose hay at the top of the stack with just his head and tuft showing, blissful.
Ned launches into a shallow blue paddling pool with all four limbs out, water leaping up in a crown shape.
A wave of water arrives at Pip, who flinches with one wing up, while Ned grins in the pool. Comic timing.
Pip stalks away from the pool with wet, spiky, indignant feathers and his tail up, Ned's splashes still going on behind him.
Pip settles into the deep cool shade under a broad leafy bush, a rich dark green pocket in an otherwise blazing-bright page.
Closing page: Pip and Ned lie flat on their backs in the shade at the end of the day, exhausted and happy, as the sun goes low and orange over the field.

the-loud-sound.alt: Pip is curled up in his ivy nest at night, one wing over his head, tiny and cosy against the deep blue dark.
The same nest is seen from outside, tiny in a huge dark garden, the oak looming sharp and startled above it as the night suddenly turns loud.
An extreme close-up of Pip's face, his eyes enormous and feathers on end, gripping the edge of the nest. The whole page is his fright.
Pip climbs cautiously out over the rim of the nest into the dark, one foot testing the branch, brave and very small.
Reveal page: Olive the owl sits on a branch above, lit by the moon, entirely unbothered and mid-hoot, big and round and slightly ridiculous.
Olive's hoot fills the page from Pip's viewpoint — close and enormous, beak wide — while Pip is a tiny silhouette in the corner of the frame.
Pip and Olive stand face to face on the branch, Pip's relief written all over him and Olive looking faintly apologetic.
Pip flies back to the nest with his shoulders down, calm now, the garden drawn soft and friendly again.
Pip is tucked back in, eyes shut, one wing over his head exactly as before — the garden quiet and still around him.
A wide, still garden at night: the oak, the nest, the moon, and Olive keeping watch as a small shape on her branch. Deeply peaceful.

moss-digs.alt: Moss the berry-brown hedgehog stands side-on with both front paws raised, showing off his claws to the reader, proud and a bit comic.
Moss is nose-down in the wet brown mud, back end up, his spikes flecked with earth.
A three-stage sequence across the page: mud flying, the hole deepening, and by the third, only Moss's back feet are left showing above the hole.
Moss's muddy face emerges from the hole with one large hazelnut held triumphantly, his eyes shining with joy.
Pip lands at speed beside the hole, wings braking, one wing up in greeting, as mud sprays towards him.
Pip sits squarely in the mud with an expression of dawning regret, while Moss looks on, thoroughly delighted.
A cutaway view of a snug round den under a tree root, with Moss inside patting the walls smooth, dry leaves lining the floor.
Closing page: Moss and Pip are asleep curled together in the den with leaves pulled over them, rain falling just outside the entrance — warm inside, cold outside.

nell-and-the-bell.alt: Nell the sunflower-yellow bee hovers beside a small bright red hand bell hanging from a twig, strong red-and-yellow colour contrast.
Nell swings into the bell with both front legs, tipping it, the ring shown as the bell blurring at its edges.
Nell swings on the bell's clapper like a rope, upside down and absolutely delighted, movement lines sweeping in an arc.
Pip arrives at a run across the grass, wings out, drawn to the noise of the bell, moving from left to right.
Moss is mostly hidden in a mud puddle, only his nose and two eyes showing, thoroughly pleased with his hiding place.
Pip skids into the same puddle at speed, feet out in front, mud flying up in a wing shape the moment before landing.
Nell hovers close by, perfectly clean and grinning down at the mud, while behind her Pip and Moss are both mud-brown and unrecognisable.
Closing page: all three are lined up together, caked in mud, the red bell hanging above them, everyone laughing. Warm and messy.

fig-in-the-sun.alt: Fig the green striped caterpillar is stretched along the top of a large mossy log, all his little legs in a neat row.
The sun is drawn large and hot at the top of the page, with the log and Fig small below it in a pool of hard light.
Fig has been warmed to a deep sunset red by the heat, still stripy underneath, looking slightly alarmed at his own colour.
Fig is fast asleep on the log, curled into a comma shape with his legs relaxed, peaceful and warm.
Pip lands on the log with a bump, tail up, waking the whole log, while Fig jolts awake mid-frame.
Pip nudges Fig with one wing while Fig grips the bark with all his legs, refusing to move — a comic tug of war.
Fig is mid-tantrum, reared up with all his legs waving, small and furious — the fuss drawn bigger than the caterpillar himself.
Closing page: Pip and Fig sit side by side on the log in the low evening sun, calm again, with long shadows behind them.

nell-and-the-wig.alt: Nell hovers in the centre of the page, her wings a soft blur, sunflower yellow against a clean pale sky.
Nell wears a ridiculous curly red wig several sizes too big, slipped over one eye — she thinks she looks magnificent.
A close view of the wig itself, bright pillar-box red and lovingly detailed with curls, resting on a twig like a hat on a stand, while Nell inspects it.
Nell zips across the page in a sharp zig-zag, the wig streaming behind her, only just hanging on.
Nell perches on a sticky jam bun almost as big as she is, her front legs deep in the jam, rich reds and golden pastry.
Pip stands on a branch with exactly six plump purple figs lined up in front of him, counting them with one wing.
Nell holds up a small paper quiz card with a big tick on it, front legs in the air in triumph, her wig askew.
Closing page: Nell and Pip are together on the branch, the wig now on Pip, jam everywhere, both helpless with laughter.

rain-and-the-moon.alt: Night rain falls hard across the whole page in long silver diagonals, the oak a dark mass behind it. No characters, just wet atmosphere.
A cutaway of the hollow in the oak shows Nell and Olive tucked up dry inside while rain streams past the opening outside — warm inside, cold outside.
A close view of a single leaf at the hollow's edge with rain running off it, Nell reaching one front leg out into the drips.
The rain is visibly thinning now — fewer, finer lines — with a pale gap opening in the cloud, in the same view as the opening page.
The clouds part to show a big bright moon, Olive's face lifting towards it, her amber eyes catching the light.
The moon is drawn very large and pale, filling most of the page, with the oak's bare top branches silhouetted across it.
Olive sits in profile on her branch, entirely still, moonlight on her round plum-coloured back. Quiet and dignified.
Closing page: Olive sits mid-hoot on the branch with Nell asleep in the crook below her, the whole wet garden shining in moonlight beneath them.

the-big-farm.alt: Ned the gold duckling walks up a rutted farm track towards a big red barn under a wide bright sky, small against the buildings ahead.
Inside the barn it is mostly dark, with one shaft of dusty light slanting through a gap in the boards and straw scattered on the floor. Ned is a small silhouette in the doorway.
Two shapes are half-seen in the barn gloom, a pig's round back and a hen's sharp outline, neither fully lit, while Ned peers at them unsure.
Ned stands outside again in a field of tall golden corn, the stalks towering over him as he looks straight up.
Moss the hedgehog pushes through the corn stalks with a leaf on his back, only half visible, while Ned spots him with delight.
At a fork in the corn rows, Moss points firmly towards the barn roof with one paw while Ned is already leaning the other way.
Ned runs flat out down a long farm track that shrinks away to a tiny point far in the distance.
At dusk, Ned curls up asleep in a straw-lined corner of the barn with one last shaft of warm light falling on him.
Closing page: the sun rises over the farm gate as Ned heads home along the track, happy and satisfied, with the barn behind him.

down-by-the-pond.alt: Ned walks down a dewy grassy slope towards the pond in the early morning, his tracks showing behind him in the wet grass.
The sun clears the hedge and spreads a bright path of light across the pond surface, with Ned a small silhouette at the water's edge.
Ned stands with his head cocked, listening, while a cow raises its head over the hedge in the middle distance on a quiet rural morning.
Close on dark soil, a small round coin lies half buried with one bright edge catching the sun, as Ned's beak reaches towards it.
A pair of hens pick busily about together on the bank, while Ned watches them with interest.
Olive the owl perches with great dignity on the back of an old wooden chair left out beside the pond.
A wide dusk view of the pond turning pink and grey, with reeds standing black against the water as everything settles for the night.
Ned turns away from the water to head home, pausing for one last look back over his shoulder, small against the big landscape.
Closing page: Olive waves from the chair and Ned waves back as he walks off up the slope, warm last light glowing on the pond behind them.

fun-at-the-fair.alt: Fig the caterpillar and Nell the bee arrive at a small country fair with bunting overhead, stripey tents and a distant big wheel.
A wide, busy fairground scene packed with stalls, flags and bunting, lights just coming on as dusk falls.
Nell hovers in front of an enormous painted fairground chair-swing, completely dwarfed by it, her front legs raised in wonder.
Looking straight up, the fairground chair-swing sits tiny at the very top of its arc against a huge darkening sky.
Fig stands braced on all his legs, his little face turned towards a cheering crowd off to the side, their arms raised.
A cheerful stallholder stands behind a steaming corn stall with cobs stacked in golden rows, warm light and steam rising.
Nell sits astride a corn cob almost as long as she is, eating along it like a tiny yellow harvester.
Fig holds up a bright red paper party hat he has won, all his legs off the ground with pride.
Closing page: Fig, still wearing his red party hat, and Nell walk home together in the dark as the fair glows small behind them.

the-best-nest.alt: Pip surveys a battered, half-collapsed nest with twigs sticking out at wrong angles, one wing on his hip as he assesses the damage.
A flashback to the same nest whole and perfect, neat, round and beautifully woven, in warm gold light.
Nell flies in carrying a single twig longer than she is, wobbling badly under its weight but determined.
Close on Pip and Nell holding one twig very carefully between them, both faces tense with concentration.
A gust of wind hits: the ivy thrashes, twigs fly out of the frame and Pip and Nell are both blown sideways.
The nest has landed in a patch of sand at the foot of the wall, twigs scattered all around it in a wide spray.
Pip sits alone beside the wreckage with his head down and shoulders low, lots of empty space around him.
Nell comes to sit beside Pip with one small leg resting on his wing, a close, warm moment as colour returns to the page.
Pip and Nell both work busily, twigs in their beak and legs, the nest visibly re-forming between them.
Closing page: the finished nest is rounder and sturdier than before, with Pip and Nell sitting together inside it in the evening sun.

frost-on-the-pond.alt: A wide winter morning view of the pond, frozen and white, with reeds stiff with frost in blue and silver light.
Ned steps onto the ice with one foot, his other foot still on the bank, an expression of doubt on his face — the instant before it all goes wrong.
Ned lies completely flat on the ice, legs splayed in every direction and his beak right on the frost.
Ned slides helplessly across the whole width of the frozen pond, still lying flat, with a look of complete resignation.
Moss bursts out of his leaf-pile den at the bank, spikes bristling, going at full hedgehog speed, which is not very fast at all.
Moss stands at the ice edge with one paw out, shouting, while Ned lies on his back some distance away, waving one foot.
Ned spins on the ice like a top, wings flung out, delighted, with circular motion lines swirling around him.
Moss slides on his tummy and Ned spins beside him, both on the ice, ice shavings flying, full of joy and movement.
Closing page: Ned and Moss head back into the warm, dark leaf den at dusk, frost still on their backs.

nells-long-trip.alt: Nell sets off from the hive behind the sunflowers, a small bee against the whole meadow spread out ahead of her.
An aerial, map-like view of the pond from above, with Nell's tiny flight path curving past it and the distance covered stretching behind.
Nell battles a strong wind, blown sideways off her course, wings straining, as the grass flattens in waves below her.
Nell lands on a bent stem, her wings drooping, every line of her posture saying how tired she is.
Close on Nell drinking a bead of dew from a leaf, restored and content after her rest.
A line of ants marches briskly up the stem past Nell in single file, completely ignoring her.
The hive comes into view over the sunflowers as Nell puts on a burst of speed towards it, sheer relief on her face.
Closing page: Nell is tucked up resting in the hive entrance at dusk, the sunflowers glowing behind her and the long trip behind her.

the-big-pie.alt: Fig stands beside a pie easily four times his own size, up on his back legs to see over the crust.
The pie is cut open to show deep purple plum filling, glossy and rich, with steam rising from it.
Nell hovers over the pie, taking a small, polite bite from the very edge, while Fig watches.
Fig and Nell are both mid-mouthful, eyes shut in complete bliss over the pie.
Fig lies curled up and resting beside the mostly-eaten pie, his middle enormously round.
Nell carefully arranges a tiny ribbon bow tie around Fig's neck while he lies there, far too full to object.
Fig stands up wearing his new bow tie, striking a dignified pose, while Nell applauds.
Closing page: Fig and Nell lie asleep together in the empty pie dish like a bed, Fig's bow tie still on, in golden evening light.

by-the-sea.alt: Pip and Ned arrive at the top of a dune with the whole sea opening up in front of them, two small figures against a big sky and big water.
Close on Ned's orange feet in clear shallow water at the shoreline, a small wave breaking over them in cool greens and blues.
Ned works through an enormous picnic, a wrapped sandwich bigger than his own head, with total commitment.
Pip sits with a small cup of tea balanced on a flat rock, one wing around it, very civilised, with steam rising.
Pip and Ned sit side by side on the sand looking out to sea, small and quiet against the wide horizon.
Ned lies on his front reading a book propped up in the sand, utterly absorbed, feet in the air behind him.
A crab scuttles sideways out of the sand with one claw raised, as Ned leaps airborne in retreat, his book flying.
A wide beach scene at golden hour, long shadows reaching across the sand as the tide comes in over their footprints.
Closing page: Pip and Ned walk back up the dune at sunset, sandy and tired, Ned still holding his book, the sea glowing orange behind them.

the-toy-boat.alt: Ned the duckling holds up a small wooden toy boat with both flippers, presenting it to the reader with enormous pride.
A close view of the boat itself: a pillar-box red hull, a white sail, and chipped paint showing it is well loved.
Ned crouches at the pond edge, lowering the boat onto the water with his tongue out in concentration as ripples spread from it.
The boat sails out across the open water, small and upright with its reflection beneath it, on a wide calm pond.
Moss arrives at the bank with his own toy, a squat wooden tug, held awkwardly in both paws — slightly embarrassed, very endearing.
The two toys collide beside a grey rock, one tipping with a small splash, while both owners' faces are caught mid-horror on the bank.
Ned, close-cropped so the alarm fills the page, looks utterly dismayed at what has happened to the toys.
Both boats bob upright again, entirely undamaged, one still gently spinning, with relief on the bank behind them.
Ned is airborne with joy, both wings up, boat clutched to his chest, water droplets flying in pure celebration.
Closing page: Ned and Moss sit close together on the bank at golden hour, with both boats out drying on the grass, warm and content.

the-bird-and-the-girl.alt: Pip is drawn small and neat on a park railing, seen against a big open park background so his smallness reads.
Pip sees a child sitting cross-legged on the grass a little way off, seen from his low viewpoint so she looks large and gentle.
The child sits on a bare patch of earth scratching a pattern in the dirt with a stick, absorbed, while Pip watches from the railing.
Pip hops down onto the grass — the brave first hop — one foot forward, wings half out, everything about him tentative.
Olive the owl lands heavily on the railing behind Pip, huge by comparison, blocking out a chunk of sky — comic size contrast.
Olive does a slow showy turn on the railing with her wings out, half a pirouette, entirely pleased with herself.
The child laughs with both birds near her — Pip on her knee, Olive on the railing — warm and gentle, with no touching of the owl.
The two birds fly away together over the park treetops, with the child waving small below them, seen from an aerial viewpoint.
Closing page: Pip and Olive are back on their own branch in the oak at sunset, the park visible far off, warm and homeward.

fun-in-the-wind.alt: The whole garden bends in a gale — the bush leans, leaves stream off the page, and washing blows horizontal on the line.
Pip clamps to a branch with both feet and both wings, tail blown straight out sideways, his eyes squeezed shut. Very funny.
Nell is blown clean off her flight path, tumbling sideways with her legs waving, drawn as a small yellow blur.
A large twig snaps off the oak and falls across the frame with leaves streaming, while both of them dive clear below it.
Pip and Nell scramble low across the grass together, using the ground for shelter, grass flattened all round them.
The garden shed appears through the wind, its door swinging to warm dark safety inside, as the pair heads for it.
Inside the shed it is a cosy clutter of flowerpots, the two of them tucked between the pots while wind howls past the window.
Closing page: the shed door is open on a completely still garden, one leaf falling gently as the pair steps out. Calm after the storm.

lunch-on-the-grass.alt: Fig and Moss lay out a small picnic on a checked cloth in the grass — cheerful and domestic.
The two of them settle on the soft grass, seen from a low viewpoint with grass blades framing the shot like a forest.
Fig holds a single potato crisp bigger than his own head, about to bite the edge — comic scale, lovely crisp texture.
Moss holds a deep purple plum in both paws, juice already on his chin, its rich colour bright against his brown spikes.
A wasp cuts across the page in a hard straight line while both picnickers freeze mid-bite, watching it go.
The wasp is gone off the edge of the frame — both of them exhale with relief, Moss's spikes settling back down.
Both of them lie flat on their backs on the cloth with full tummies, hats over their eyes, deeply asleep in the dappled shade.
Closing page: the empty cloth with crumbs and a plum stone, late afternoon light across the grass, two contented shapes asleep beside it.

paws-by-the-pond.alt: Ned stares down at a single large paw print in the mud, crisp and clear and considerably bigger than his own foot.
A close-up of the print: four toe pads and a heel pressed into wet brown mud, with water gathering inside it.
Ned looks around the reeds with wide eyes, imagining a faint fox shape suggested in the shadows behind the stems.
Ned crawls forward on his belly through the grass in full stealth mode, only his eyes above the stems. Very funny.
A single curved claw is caught on a grass stem, gleaming and drawn large, with Ned's beak just inches from it.
A big fat tabby cat is revealed lying in the sun beside the pond, entirely harmless and half asleep, as Ned slumps with relief.
The cat is mid-yawn, an enormous pink mouth and curled tongue, teeth on full display but comic rather than scary.
Ned yawns back at the cat in unconscious imitation — the two of them mirroring each other. Charming.
Closing page: pale dawn light falls over the pond, the cat asleep, as Ned waddles off to bed with his eyes already closing.

the-new-stew.alt: Nell the bee stands beside a brand new cooking pot, gleaming and far too big for her, admiring her own reflection in it.
Nell is perched on the pot's rim, stirring with a long twig as steam rises past her in warm kitchen-ish light.
Fig blows hard across a spoonful of stew, cheeks out, with the steam bending away from him in comic effort.
Fig recoils with his mouth open and tongue out — the stew is clearly far too hot.
A close view of the stew's surface with exactly a few round green peas floating in it, drawn countably. Rich and appetising.
Nell has an enormous cup, drinking with both front legs round it, almost disappearing behind it. Funny scale.
Both of them sit on the pot rim with full bowls, eyes shut in appreciation — warm and companionable.
Closing page: the pot is scraped completely clean and gleaming, two very round friends asleep against it in cosy evening light.

toes-in-the-mud.alt: A close view of Ned's webbed feet completely caked in thick brown mud, seen from above, as he looks down at them unimpressed.
Ned hops on one foot clutching the other, beak open, having stubbed his toe on a half-buried stone. Very funny.
Inside the garden shed, Pip holds up an old wooden-handled hoe far bigger than himself, presenting the solution.
Ned drags the hoe through the mud with both wings, leaning right back into the effort, cutting a deep furrow.
A deer bounds across the far end of the garden, legs stretched, seen through the gap in the hedge — elegant and sudden.
The deer runs at full speed in the middle distance, all four feet off the ground, while both friends watch, stopped mid-action.
A close view of the deer's slender feet touching the ground and leaving almost no mark, contrasted with Ned's great muddy prints beside them.
Closing page: Ned and Pip sit together in the evening sun, feet clean now, the dug bed neat behind them. Satisfied.

the-big-haul.alt: Nell the bee grips a rope attached to a large net at the pond edge, leaning back with all her weight — she is tiny, the net is not.
The rope is stretched bar-straight and quivering — the net is snagged on something under the water.
Moss arrives and takes hold of the rope behind Nell, both of them leaning back in a line — teamwork.
Both of them strain with feet dug in, faces screwed up with effort, the rope creeping in inch by inch.
The net is finally out on the bank, bulging with weed, an old boot and a great many small treasures — rewarding to pore over.
Nell does a somersault in mid-air out of sheer delight, drawn as a looping motion arc with a yellow blur at the end.
Moss attempts the same somersault and gets it entirely wrong — mid-tumble, legs everywhere, spikes bristling. Hilarious.
Closing page: the pair sit on the upturned boot beside their haul at sunset, exhausted and triumphant, warm gold across the pond.

pips-listening-walk.alt: Wide dawn view of the garden. Pip the small sandy-brown sparrow sits on the edge of his ivy nest above the shed roof, head cocked and one wing raised, soft gold morning light around him.
Close view of a weathered wooden garden gate swinging on a rusty hinge, with Pip perched on the top bar bobbing with the movement, eyes wide and delighted.
Close view of the corrugated shed roof with fine drizzle bouncing off it, while Pip shelters dry under the guttering, watching the rain.
Pip peers into the dark bottom of a leafy hedge, tail up, curious and a tiny bit unsure, with only a glimpse of something hidden in the shadows.
Moss the hedgehog steps out of the hedge blinking, a single yellow leaf balanced on his snout, while Pip hops back in friendly surprise, wings half open.
Looking straight up the trunk of the old oak to Olive the owl perched far above on a branch, beak open mid-hoot, with a great deal of empty sky around her.
Pip curled up asleep and content in his twiggy ivy nest, evening light going pink behind him, with the faint ghosted shapes of the day's sounds around the edge of the page.

nells-noisy-hive.alt: Nell the bee hovers in front of a tidy hive behind tall sunflowers, holding an empty jam jar like a conductor, her tuft of fluff sticking up with effort.
Nell strikes two dry twigs together, a tiny puff of dust at the moment of contact, tall sunflower stems making warm vertical stripes behind her.
A dented tin can lies on its side as Nell drums its base with both front legs, the first BOOM sending a startled ladybird flying off it in playful chaos.
Ned the duckling slaps the reedy pond edge with one flat webbed foot, a wide splash ring spreading out and water droplets caught in the air, looking extremely pleased with himself.
Nell spins in mid-air with all six legs in different positions, a diagonal blur of movement lines, while Ned watches with his beak open.
Nell is frozen with one leg raised like a conductor's baton, Ned's foot half lifted and the tin still rocking — a very still, quiet composition.
A calm closing page: Nell sits on the upturned tin at dusk with Ned beside her, both looking out at the darkening garden in warm low light.

moss-and-the-rhyme-pot.alt: Under the wooden garden bench, Moss the hedgehog leans nose-deep into a chipped terracotta pot surrounded by dry leaf bedding, a slice of light falling across the scene.
Moss drops a small picture-card of a cat into the pot with great ceremony, while Fig the caterpillar watches from above, unconvinced, one eyebrow raised.
A mossy log tips into the pot on one side while a startled frog sits mid-blink on the pot's rim on the other — a log went in, and a frog came out.

A comically enormous pale moon squeezes up out of a small flower pot, filling the top half of the page, with a wooden spoon discarded below. Fig stands with his legs on his hips, exasperated, while Moss is delighted.
Fig emerges from the pot wearing a ridiculous curly wig several sizes too big, his green stripes still showing underneath, while Moss laughs so hard his spikes have gone flat.
A wide, quiet closing view from outside the bench: two small friends sitting side by side with the pot between them, the real moon high above the garden in deep evening blue.

olives-sound-game.alt: Olive the owl perches importantly on a low branch, one wing extended like a teacher, while Pip and Ned sit attentively on the grass below her.
Pip stands tall and proud on a stone, chest puffed out, with a small pond, a flower pot and a single petal drawn around him like a border.
Ned the duckling goes cross-eyed trying to look at his own beak, one webbed foot lifted, with a small nest and a bush drawn around him in a border.
Olive holds one acorn in each foot, slowly pulling them apart, while Pip and Ned lean in close, ready, in a slightly magical moment.
Three separate acorn shapes float apart across the page, with a warm round sun only faintly visible beginning to show through behind them.
Four pieces of twig float apart in a curve, with the faint outline of a nest beginning to assemble itself behind them.
Pip tumbles backwards off the branch with his legs in the air and total astonishment on his face, feathers everywhere, while Ned laughs and Olive sits entirely unbothered, still holding her acorns.
Olive scratches a single simple mark into the bare earth with one claw — just a mark, not a letter — while Pip and Ned look down at it together in the last quiet light of the day.

the-longest-day.alt: Very early summer morning, the sun already high over the garden, while Pip squints one eye open in disbelief from the ivy nest.
Ned the duckling stands on the pond edge in a running pose, chest out and utterly convinced of himself, while a frog and a fish in the water look distinctly unimpressed.
Pip perches on a stone with both wings clamped over his ears, while Ned, drawn slightly bigger than life, quacks with his beak wide open — a comic size contrast.
Moss the hedgehog ambles along a garden path with a leaf on his back, taking his time, while Pip and Ned are already tiny in the distance ahead.
Looking straight up the huge trunk of the old oak, with Pip just a small speck near the very top, wings spread.
A three-step sequence: Ned scrambling onto a low branch, then slipping to a lower one, then sitting in the grass with a leaf on his head — the same pose, three funny stages.
All three friends squeeze together into a strip of deep cool shade under the hedge, panting slightly, with the rest of the page bleached bright by the heat.
Moss is curled into a ball fast asleep with Pip asleep on top of him, and Ned collapsed asleep in a silly heap beside them, in the late evening light.

ned-is-unsure.alt: Ned stares at a small empty dip in the mud at the pond edge where a stone clearly used to sit, shoulders and beak down on a flat overcast page.
The same empty mud dip, drawn closer and larger, with only a faint ghosted outline of where the stone used to be — quiet and a little eerie.
Olive the owl sits calmly on a branch with one wing raised in warning, while below her Ned is already chest-deep in the pond, rings spreading out around him.
Ned stands dripping on the bank, his down plastered flat so he looks half his normal size, while Nell the bee hovers nearby trying hard not to laugh.
Nell hovers with one leg pointing firmly down, absolutely certain, while Ned looks up at her with dawning hope.
Nell pulls the reed stems apart like curtains while Olive steps into the shallows with one foot lifted high, an expression of deep distaste on her face.
The stone sits half buried in dark mud, one polished grey curve catching the light, as Ned's face comes right up close to it, eyes enormous.
Ned sits squarely and smugly on top of the stone at the water's edge, wings folded and immovable, with Nell and Olive behind him looking amused in the late gold light.

jumping-and-splashing.alt: Ned is mid-air over the pond in a tucked jump, legs pulled in and sheer joy on his face, with the log and the rock he has already used below him.
Pip sits on a fence post above the pond, entirely dry and radiating disapproval, while Ned's splash reaches almost but not quite up to him.
Fig the caterpillar is stretched full length along a big warm leaf in the sun, all his legs relaxed, eyes shut, extremely comfortable.
The moment of impact: a wall of water arrives at the fence post and Pip erupts in a flap of shocked feathers with one indignant open beak.
Pip hops furiously along the fence rail, wings out, water running off his tail feathers, while Ned sits innocently in the pond below.
Fig tumbles sideways off the leaf, all his legs waving, with a small splash below, while Pip and Ned both stop to look.
Fig lies on the bank in a wet, bedraggled, grinning heap, with Ned and Pip either side of him, both dripping too — all three friends again in the warm evening light.
A joyful full-page spread of all three friends in mid-air over the pond at once, Pip highest of all with his wings spread wide and his eyes shut in delight, a big splash forming below.

boxes-and-bushes.alt: Moss the hedgehog sits beside six battered wooden crates on the dewy morning grass, all clearly empty, one lying on its side, peering hopefully into the nearest one.
Nell hovers with both front legs flung wide in an exaggerated 'this many' gesture, while Moss looks thoroughly sceptical.
A thin scrubby bush bears exactly five countable nuts, while Nell hovers a bit lower now, sheepish, and Moss stays entirely deadpan.
A tall dense bush fills the page, heavy with nuts drawn in loving detail, while Moss stands at the bottom looking up with his mouth open.
Two halves of the same picture: on the left the crates are filling up with nuts, and on the right the same branch is already stripped bare and springing back.
Olive the owl arrives importantly with two chipped china dishes balanced on her wings, while Moss and Nell exchange a look.
Moss sits among the crates with an enormously round tummy and one last nut in his paw, Nell and Olive on either side of him, very funny.
The three friends walk home at dusk under a warm purple evening sky, Nell towing one dish, Olive carrying the other, and Moss rolling along behind like a nut himself.

the-cake-on-the-lake.alt: Nell the bee beams beside a small lopsided cake on a leaf plate, decorated with a scatter of seeds, in warm gold light.
Nell hovers along carrying the leaf plate while Moss plods beside her at a fraction of the speed, tongue out with effort, along a long path.
Moss is stuck to his middle in thick brown mud, spikes flat with dismay, holding the cake plate up high and clean above his head.
The instant of disaster: Ned reaches for the plate, one foot slips, and the cake sails off in a graceful arc towards the water while everyone watches in horror.
A calm wide view of the still lake surface with the small cake floating perfectly upright in the middle, soft reflections all around — absurd and lovely.
Another duck paddles hopefully towards the floating cake, but Ned sits in the water between them with his wings spread wide and his beak set — territorial and hilarious.
The three friends sit together on a flat wet rock in the shallows with the rescued cake between them, damp and happy, sharing it in crumbs in the late afternoon light.

five-white-kites.alt: Pip stands on a breezy hilltop holding five kite strings, five white diamond kites climbing above him against a huge pale blue sky.
Fig lies flat on the grass gripping a stem with all his legs, staring up with deep suspicion at kites that loom enormous above him.
A close two-shot: Pip patient and reasonable, Fig unconvinced, with one kite string coiling near him like a snake — clearly why he is suspicious.
The kites are tiny and far off near the top of the page, strings stretched taut, grass flattened below as Pip leans back hard against the pull of the wind.
A snapped string whips loose and one kite tumbles away into the distance over the treetops, getting smaller, while Pip's expression is stricken and the other four kites stay up.
Olive the owl flies at full speed, wings swept back, absolutely determined, with streaks of movement behind her — genuinely impressive and slightly frightening.
Olive lands with the muddy kite held in one foot, entirely unruffled, delivering her report while Pip and Fig look up at her with enormous respect.
Fig sits on the grass with one kite string wound firmly around his middle, a small white kite bobbing above him, intense concentration and secret delight on his face in the final warm evening light.

the-blue-phone.alt: Nell the bee hovers over an old blue mobile phone lying in long grass, dew on the screen, front legs tucked behind her back like a detective.
Pip lands beside the phone, head tilted right over to look at it, while Nell shrugs mid-air — both of them completely baffled.
Olive the owl stands over the phone in full lecturing mode, one wing raised, her round shape filling the frame, while Pip and Nell listen in total faith.
Nell hovers with the phone held up to where her ear would be, eyes shut, listening hard, while Olive looks on from the background, put out.
Two halves of the same picture: Olive's foot fills a blurry phone screen on the left, while Nell talks earnestly into a completely blank screen on the right — both absurd, both committed.
The phone suddenly lights up and rings in the grass, sending all three friends flying off in different directions in a big comic burst of movement.
The phone screen shows a simple picture of a smiling child, the three friends crowded small round it looking in, a soft blue glow on their faces.
The blue phone sits back in the grass exactly where it started, while the three small friends walk away together into the quiet evening.
